title: Cookie smuggling, tossing and strict Cookie-header parsing
attackSurface: A browser-supplied Cookie request header parsed by a server-side application

references.note: Jetty quoted-cookie parsing allowed cookies to be smuggled inside other cookies

hostile.title: Cookie tossing duplicate
hostile.why: Duplicate names make subdomain-injected cookies ambiguous

hostile.title: CRLF Cookie-header split
hostile.why: Line breaks in a serialized cookie header enable request or response splitting

hostile.title: Quoted cookie smuggling
hostile.why: CVE-2023-26049 style semicolon smuggling through quoted values

hostile.title: Encoded line-feed smuggling
hostile.why: Percent-decoded control characters must not reach downstream parsers

hostile.title: Prototype-polluting cookie name
hostile.why: Cookie names become object keys in many JavaScript parsers

hostile.title: Comma delimiter confusion
hostile.why: Comma-joined cookie headers can be interpreted differently by intermediaries

hostile.title: NUL byte cookie value
hostile.why: NUL bytes can split JavaScript and native parser views

benign.title: Percent-encoded data
benign.why: Valid percent escapes preserved as data

benign.title: Balanced quoted value
benign.why: Balanced quotes are valid cookie-octet structure

benign.title: Equals inside value
benign.why: Additional equals signs are data after the first separator

benign.title: Object-method cookie name
benign.why: Names that collide with Object methods must remain isolated data

benign.title: Transport whitespace
benign.why: Multiple spaces after a semicolon are valid transport whitespace
